title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of John Wesley's sermon, Upon Our Lord's Sermon on the Mount, Discourse Eight. It is the sermon as printed in John Wesley's 1771 Works. Rendered in modern English.

title: Treasures upon earth
english: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal. Matthew 6:19.

title: Treasures in heaven
english: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust corrupts, and where thieves do not break through nor steal. Matthew 6:20.

title: Where your treasure is
english: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Matthew 6:21.

title: The single eye
english: The light of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is single, your whole body shall be full of light. Matthew 6:22.

title: How great is that darkness
english: But if your eye is evil, your whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is within you is darkness, how great is that darkness. Matthew 6:23.

title: Purity in ordinary business
english: From those which are commonly termed religious actions, and which are real branches of true religion where they spring from a pure and holy intention and are performed in a manner suitable to it, our Lord proceeds to the actions of common life, and shows that the same purity of intention is as indispensably required in our ordinary business as in giving alms, or fasting, or prayer.

title: A proper offering to God
english: And without question the same purity of intention which makes our alms and devotions acceptable must also make our labor or employment a proper offering to God. If a man pursues his business, that he may raise himself to a state of figure and riches in the world, he is no longer serving God in his employment, and has no more title to a reward from God than he who gives alms that he may be seen, or prays that he may be heard of men. For vain and earthly designs are no more allowable in our employments than in our alms and devotions. They are not only evil when they mix with our good works, with our religious actions, but they have the same evil nature when they enter into the common business of our employments. If it were allowable to pursue them in our worldly employments, it would be allowable to pursue them in our devotions. But as our alms and devotions are not an acceptable service but when they proceed from a pure intention, so our common employment cannot be reckoned a service to him but when it is performed with the same piety of heart.

title: The eye is the intention
english: This our blessed Lord declares in the liveliest manner, in those strong and comprehensive words which he explains, enforces, and enlarges upon throughout this whole chapter. The light of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is single, your whole body shall be full of light. But if your eye is evil, your whole body shall be full of darkness (Matthew 6:22-23). The eye is the intention: what the eye is to the body, the intention is to the soul. As the one guides all the motions of the body, so does the other those of the soul. This eye of the soul is then said to be single when it looks at one thing only, when we have no other design but to know God and Jesus Christ whom he has sent (John 17:3), to know him with suitable affections, loving him as he has loved us, to please God in all things, to serve God (as we love him) with all our heart and mind and soul and strength, and to enjoy God in all and above all things, in time and in eternity.

title: Full of divine knowledge
english: If your eye is thus single, thus fixed on God, your whole body shall be full of light. Your whole body, all that is guided by the intention, as the body is by the eye. All you are, all you do: your desires, tempers, affections, your thoughts and words and actions. The whole of these shall be full of light, full of true, divine knowledge. This is the first thing we may here understand by light. In his light you shall see light (Psalm 36:9). He who of old commanded light to shine out of darkness shall shine in your heart (2 Corinthians 4:6). He shall enlighten the eyes of your understanding with the knowledge of the glory of God (Ephesians 1:18). His Spirit shall reveal to you the deep things of God (1 Corinthians 2:10). The inspiration of the Holy One shall give you understanding and cause you to know wisdom secretly (Psalm 51:6). Yes, the anointing which you receive of him shall abide in you and teach you of all things (1 John 2:27).

title: Clouds and doubts vanish
english: How does experience confirm this? Even after God has opened the eyes of our understanding, if we seek or desire anything else than God, how soon is our foolish heart darkened? Then clouds again rest upon our souls. Doubts and fears again overwhelm us. We are tossed to and fro and know not what to do, or which is the path wherein we should go. But when we desire and seek nothing but God, clouds and doubts vanish away. We who were once darkness are now light in the Lord (Ephesians 5:8). The night now shines as the day, and we find the path of the upright is light. God shows us the path wherein we should go and makes plain the way before our face.

title: Full of holiness
english: The second thing which we may here understand by light is holiness. While you seek God in all things, you shall find him in all, the fountain of all holiness, continually filling you with his own likeness, with justice, mercy, and truth. While you look to Jesus and him alone, you shall be filled with the mind that was in him (Philippians 2:5). Your soul shall be renewed day by day after the image of him who created it (Colossians 3:10). If the eye of your mind is not removed from him, if you endure seeing him who is invisible (Hebrews 11:27), and seeking nothing else in heaven or earth, then as you behold the glory of the Lord you shall be transformed into the same image, from glory to glory, by the Spirit of the Lord (2 Corinthians 3:18).

title: The fruits of holiness
english: And it is also matter of daily experience that by grace we are thus saved through faith. It is by faith that the eye of the mind is opened to see the light of the glorious love of God. And as long as it is steadily fixed upon it, on God in Christ reconciling the world to himself (2 Corinthians 5:19), we are more and more filled with the love of God and man, with meekness, gentleness, long-suffering, with all the fruits of holiness which are through Christ Jesus to the glory of God the Father (Philippians 1:11).

title: Full of happiness
english: This light which fills him who has a single eye implies, thirdly, happiness as well as holiness. Surely light is sweet, and a pleasant thing it is to see the sun (Ecclesiastes 11:7). But how much more to see the Sun of Righteousness continually shining upon the soul? And if there is any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any peace that passes all understanding, if any rejoicing in hope of the glory of God (Philippians 4:4-7), they all belong to him whose eye is single. Thus is his whole body full of light. He walks in the light as God is in the light, rejoicing evermore, praying without ceasing, and in everything giving thanks (1 Thessalonians 5:16-18), enjoying whatever is the will of God concerning him in Christ Jesus.

title: No medium
english: But if your eye is evil, your whole body shall be full of darkness. If your eye is evil: we see there is no medium between a single and an evil eye. If the eye is not single, then it is evil. If the intention in whatever we do is not singly to God, if we seek anything else, then our mind and conscience are defiled (Titus 1:15).

title: Any other end than God
english: Our eye therefore is evil if in anything we do we aim at any other end than God, if we have any view but to know and to love God, to please and serve him in all things, if we have any other design than to enjoy God, to be happy in him both now and forever.

title: Full of uncertainty
english: If your eye is not singly fixed on God, your whole body shall be full of darkness. The veil shall still remain on your heart (2 Corinthians 3:15). Your mind shall be more and more blinded by the god of this world, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ should shine upon you (2 Corinthians 4:4). You will be full of ignorance and error touching the things of God, not being able to receive or discern them. And even when you have some desire to serve God, you will be full of uncertainty as to the manner of serving him, finding doubts and difficulties on every side and not seeing any way to escape.

title: Conversation evil as well as heart
english: Yes, if your eye is not single, if you seek any of the things of earth, you shall be full of ungodliness and unrighteousness, your desires, tempers, affections being all out of course, being all dark and vile and vain. And your conduct will be evil as well as your heart, not seasoned with salt or fit to minister grace to the hearers (Ephesians 4:29), but idle, unprofitable, corrupt, grievous to the Holy Spirit of God.

title: No rest but in God
english: Both destruction and unhappiness are in your ways, for the way of peace have you not known (Romans 3:16-17). There is no peace, no settled, solid peace, for those who know not God. There is no true nor lasting content for any who do not seek him with their whole heart. While you aim at any of the things that perish, all that comes is vanity. Yes, not only vanity but vexation of spirit, and that both in the pursuit and the enjoyment also. You walk indeed in a vain shadow and disquiet yourself in vain (Psalm 39:6). You walk in darkness that may be felt. Sleep on, but you cannot take your rest. The dreams of life can give pain, and that you know, but ease they cannot give. There is no rest, in this world or the world to come, but only in God the center of spirits.

title: The smoke of the pit
english: If the light which is in you is darkness, how great is that darkness. If the intention which ought to enlighten the whole soul, to fill it with knowledge and love and peace, and which in fact does so as long as it is single, as long as it aims at God alone, if this is darkness, if it aims at anything besides God, and consequently covers the soul with darkness instead of light, with ignorance and error, with sin and misery: O how great is that darkness. It is the very smoke which ascends out of the bottomless pit (Revelation 9:2). It is the essential night which reigns in the lowest deep, in the land of the shadow of death.

title: Your eye is evil
english: Therefore lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal. If you do, it is plain your eye is evil. It is not singly fixed on God. Matthew 6:19.

title: The Heathen keep this command
english: With regard to most of the commandments of God, whether relating to the heart or life, the Heathen of Africa or America stand much on a level with those who are called Christians. The Christians observe them (a few only being excepted) very nearly as much as the Heathen. For instance, the generality of the natives of England, commonly called Christians, are as sober and as temperate as the generality of the Heathen near the Cape of Good Hope. And so the Dutch or French Christians are as humble and as chaste as the Choctaw or Cherokee Indians. It is not easy to say, when we compare the bulk of the nations in Europe with those in America, whether the superiority lies on the one side or the other. At least the American has not much the advantage. But we cannot affirm this with regard to the command now before us. Here the Heathen have far the preeminence. He desires and seeks nothing more than plain food to eat and plain clothing to put on. And he seeks this only from day to day. He reserves, he lays up nothing, unless it be as much corn at one season of the year as he will need before that season returns. This command therefore the Heathen, though they know it not, do constantly and punctually observe. They lay up for themselves no treasures upon earth, no stores of purple or fine linen, of gold or silver, which either moth or rust may corrupt, or thieves break through and steal. But how do the Christians observe what they profess to receive as a command of the most high God? Not at all, not in any degree, no more than if no such command had ever been given to man. Even the good Christians, as they are accounted by others as well as themselves, pay no manner of regard to it. It might as well be still hidden in its original Greek, for any notice they take of it. In what Christian city do you find 1 man of 500 who makes the least scruple of laying up just as much treasure as he can, of increasing his goods just as far as he is able? There are indeed those who would not do this unjustly. There are many who will neither rob nor steal, and some who will not defraud their neighbor, indeed who will not gain either by his ignorance or necessity. But this is quite another point. Even these do not scruple the thing but the manner of it. They do not scruple the laying up treasures upon earth but the laying them up by dishonesty. They do not start at disobeying Christ but at a breach of Heathen morality. So that even these honest men do no more obey this command than a highwayman or a housebreaker. Indeed, they never designed to obey it. From their youth up it never entered into their thoughts. They were bred up by their Christian parents, masters, and friends without any instruction at all concerning it, unless it were this: to break it as soon and as much as they could, and to continue breaking it to their life's end.

title: Spiritual infatuation
english: There is no one instance of spiritual infatuation in the world which is more amazing than this. Most of these very men read or hear the Bible read, many of them every Lord's day. They have read or heard these words a hundred times, and yet never suspect that they are themselves condemned by them, any more than by those which forbid parents to offer up their sons or daughters to Moloch (Deuteronomy 18:10).

title: The scales from their eyes
english: O that God would speak to these miserable self-deceivers with his own voice, his mighty voice, that they may at last awake out of the snare of the devil (2 Timothy 2:26), and the scales may fall from their eyes (Acts 9:18).

title: What is laying up treasures
english: Do you ask what it is to lay up treasures on earth? It will be needful to examine this thoroughly. And let us first observe what is not forbidden in this command, that we may then clearly discern what is.

title: Owe no man anything
english: We are not forbidden in this command, first, to provide things honest in the sight of all men (Romans 12:17), to provide that with which we may render to all their due, whatever they can justly demand of us. So far from it that we are taught of God to owe no man anything (Romans 13:8). We ought therefore to use all diligence in our calling in order to owe no man anything, this being no other than a plain law of common justice, which our Lord came not to destroy but to fulfill (Matthew 5:17).

title: Needful for the body
english: Neither, secondly, does he here forbid the providing for ourselves such things as are needful for the body: a sufficiency of plain, wholesome food to eat, and clean clothing to put on. Yes, it is our duty, so far as God puts it into our power, to provide these things also, to the end we may eat our own bread and be burdensome to no man (2 Thessalonians 3:8).

title: Provide for our children
english: Nor yet are we forbidden, thirdly, to provide for our children and for those of our own household. This also it is our duty to do, even upon principles of Heathen morality. Every man ought to provide the plain necessaries of life for his own wife and children, and to put them into a capacity of providing these for themselves when he is gone hence and is no more seen. I say, of providing these, the plain necessaries of life, not delicacies, not superfluities, and that by their diligent labor, for it is no man's duty to furnish them any more than himself with the means either of luxury or idleness. But if any man does not provide thus far for his own children (as well as for the widows of his own house, of whom primarily Saint Paul is speaking in those well-known words to Timothy), he has practically denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever, or Heathen (1 Timothy 5:8).

title: Carrying on our business
english: Lastly, we are not forbidden in these words to lay up from time to time what is needful for the carrying on our worldly business, in such a measure and degree as is sufficient to answer the foregoing purposes: in such a measure as first to owe no man anything, secondly to procure for ourselves the necessaries of life, and thirdly to furnish those of our own house with them while we live, and with the means of procuring them when we are gone to God.

title: What is forbidden
english: We may now clearly discern (unless we are unwilling to discern it) what that is which is forbidden here. It is the designedly procuring more of this world's goods than will answer the foregoing purposes, the laboring after a larger measure of worldly substance, a larger increase of gold and silver. The laying up any more than these ends require is what is here expressly and absolutely forbidden. If the words have any meaning at all, it must be this, for they are capable of no other. Consequently whoever he is that, owing no man anything and having food and clothing for himself and his household, together with a sufficiency to carry on his worldly business so far as answers these reasonable purposes, whoever, I say, being already in these circumstances, seeks a still larger portion on earth, he lives in an open, habitual denial of the Lord who bought him (2 Peter 2:1). He has practically denied the faith and is worse than an African or American unbeliever.

title: You have gained hell-fire
english: Hear this, all you who dwell in the world and love the world wherein you dwell. You may be highly esteemed of men, but you are an abomination in the sight of God. How long shall your souls cleave to the dust (Psalm 119:25)? How long will you load yourselves with thick clay (Habakkuk 2:6)? When will you awake and see that the open, speculative Heathen are nearer the kingdom of heaven than you? When will you be persuaded to choose the better part, that which cannot be taken away from you (Luke 10:42)? When will you seek only to lay up treasures in heaven, renouncing, dreading, abhorring all other? If you aim at laying up treasures on earth, you are not barely losing your time and spending your strength for that which is not bread (Isaiah 55:2). For what is the fruit, if you succeed? You have murdered your own soul. You have extinguished the last spark of spiritual life in it. Now indeed, in the midst of life you are in death. You are a living man but a dead Christian. For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also (Matthew 6:21). Your heart is sunk into the dust. Your soul cleaves to the ground. Your affections are set not on things above but on things of the earth (Colossians 3:2), on poor husks that may poison but cannot satisfy an everlasting spirit made for God. Your love, your joy, your desire are all placed on the things which perish in the using. You have thrown away the treasure in heaven. God and Christ are lost. You have gained riches and hell-fire.

title: The camel and the needle
english: O how hardly shall those who have riches enter into the kingdom of God (Mark 10:23). When our Lord's disciples were astonished at his speaking thus, he was so far from retracting it that he repeated the same important truth in stronger terms than before. It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God (Mark 10:25). How hard is it for those whose every word is applauded not to be wise in their own eyes (Proverbs 26:12). How hard for them not to think themselves better than the poor, base, uneducated herd of men. How hard not to seek happiness in their riches or in things dependent upon them, in gratifying the desire of the flesh, the desire of the eye, or the pride of life (1 John 2:16). O you rich, how can you escape the damnation of hell (Matthew 23:33)? Only with God all things are possible (Mark 10:27).

title: Those who desire to be rich
english: And even if you do not succeed, what is the fruit of your endeavoring to lay up treasures on earth? Those who desire to be rich (they who desire, who endeavor after it, whether they succeed or not) fall into temptation and a snare, a trap of the devil, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, desires with which reason has nothing to do, such as properly belong not to rational and immortal beings but only to the brute beasts which have no understanding, which drown men in destruction and perdition, in present and eternal misery (1 Timothy 6:9). Let us but open our eyes and we may daily see the melancholy proofs of this: men who, desiring, resolving to be rich, coveting after money, the root of all evil, have already pierced themselves through with many sorrows (1 Timothy 6:10) and anticipated the hell to which they are going.

title: A covenant with death
english: The cautiousness with which the apostle here speaks is highly observable. He does not affirm this absolutely of the rich, for a man may possibly be rich without any fault of his, by an overruling providence preventing his own choice. But he affirms it of those who desire or seek to be rich. Riches, dangerous as they are, do not always drown men in destruction and perdition. But the desire of riches does. Those who calmly desire and deliberately seek to attain them, whether they do in fact gain the world or not, do infallibly lose their own souls. These are those who sell him who bought them with his blood for a few pieces of gold or silver. These enter into a covenant with death and hell (Isaiah 28:15), and their covenant shall stand. For they are daily making themselves fit to partake of their inheritance with the devil and his angels.

title: A generation of vipers
english: O who shall warn this generation of vipers to flee from the wrath to come (Matthew 3:7)? Not those who lie at their gate or cringe at their feet, desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fall from their tables (Luke 16:21). Not those who court their favor or fear their frown, none of those who mind earthly things (Philippians 3:19). But if there is a Christian upon earth, if there is a man who has overcome the world, who desires nothing but God and fears none but him who is able to destroy both body and soul in hell (Matthew 10:28): you, O man of God, speak and spare not, lift up your voice like a trumpet (Isaiah 58:1). Cry aloud and show these honorable sinners the desperate condition in which they stand. It may be, 1 in 1,000 may have ears to hear, may arise and shake himself from the dust, may break loose from these chains that bind him to the earth, and at length lay up treasures in heaven.

title: Be not high-minded
english: And if it should be that one of these, by the mighty power of God, awoke and asked: What must I do to be saved (Acts 16:30)? The answer, according to the oracles of God, is clear, full, and express. God does not say to you: Sell all that you have. Indeed he who sees the hearts of men saw it needful to enjoin this in one peculiar case, that of the young rich ruler (Mark 10:21). But he never laid it down for a general rule to all rich men in all succeeding generations. His general direction is, first: Do not be high-minded (1 Timothy 6:17). God sees not as man sees (1 Samuel 16:7). He esteems you not for your riches, for your grandeur or equipage, for any qualification or accomplishment which is directly or indirectly owing to your wealth, which can be bought or procured by it. All these are with him as dung and dross. Let them be so with you also. Beware you do not think yourself to be one jot wiser or better for all these things. Weigh yourself in another balance. Estimate yourself only by the measure of faith and love which God has given you. If you have more of the knowledge and love of God than he, you are on this account, and no other, wiser and better, more valuable and honorable than he who is with the dogs of your flock (Job 30:1). But if you have not this treasure, you are more foolish, more vile, more truly contemptible, I will not say than the lowest servant under your roof, but than the beggar laid at your gate, full of sores (Luke 16:20).

title: Trust not in riches
english: Secondly: Do not trust in uncertain riches (1 Timothy 6:17). Do not trust in them for help, and do not trust in them for happiness.

title: No help in gold
english: First, do not trust in them for help. You are miserably mistaken if you look for this in gold or silver. These are no more able to set you above the world than to set you above the devil. Know that both the world and the prince of this world laugh at all such preparations against them. These will little avail in the day of trouble, even if they remain in the trying hour. But it is not certain that they will, for how often do they make themselves wings and fly away (Proverbs 23:5)? But if not, what support will they afford even in the ordinary troubles of life? The desire of your eyes, the wife of your youth, your son, your only son, or the friend who was as your own soul, is taken away at a stroke. Will your riches reanimate the breathless clay or call back its late inhabitant? Will they secure you from sickness, diseases, pain? Do these visit the poor only? No. He who feeds your flocks or tills your ground has less sickness and pain than you. He is more rarely visited by these unwelcome guests, and if they come there at all, they are more easily driven away from the little cottage than from the cloud-topped palaces. And during the time that your body is chastened with pain or consumes away with pining sickness, how do your treasures help you? Let the poor Heathen answer.

title: Pictures to sore eyes
english: As painted pictures are to bleary eyes, poultices to the gout, or music to ears aching with gathered filth, so are riches to the sick and sorrowing man.

title: You are to die
english: But there is at hand a greater trouble than all these. You are to die. You are to sink into dust, to return to the ground from which you were taken, to mix with common clay. Your body is to go to the earth as it was, while your spirit returns to God who gave it (Ecclesiastes 12:7). And the time draws on. The years slide away with a swift though silent pace. Perhaps your day is far spent. The noon of life is past, and the evening shadows begin to rest upon you. You feel in yourself sure-approaching decay. The springs of life wear away apace. Now what help is there in your riches? Do they sweeten death? Do they endear that solemn hour? Quite the reverse. O death, how bitter are you to a man who lives at rest in his possessions? How unacceptable to him is that awful sentence: This night shall your soul be required of you (Luke 12:20). Or will they prevent the unwelcome stroke or prolong the dreadful hour? Can they deliver your soul that it should not see death? Can they restore the years that are past? Can they add to your appointed time a month, a day, an hour, a moment? Or will the good things you have chosen for your portion here follow you over the great gulf? Not so. Naked you came into this world. Naked must you return (Job 1:21).

title: None but the cypress
english: Earth must be left, and home, and your pleasing wife. And of these trees which you tend, none but the hated cypress shall follow its short-lived master.

title: Too plain to be denied
english: Surely, were not these truths too plain to be observed because they are too plain to be denied, no man who is to die could possibly trust for help in uncertain riches.

title: No happiness in riches
english: And do not trust in them for happiness. For here also they will be found deceitful upon the weights (Proverbs 11:1). Indeed this every reasonable man may infer from what has been observed already. For if neither thousands of gold and silver, nor any of the advantages or pleasures purchased by them, can prevent our being miserable, it evidently follows they cannot make us happy. What happiness can they afford to him who in the midst of all is constrained to cry out:

title: Care around the gilded roofs
english: To my new courts sad thought does still repair, and round my gilded roofs hangs hovering care.

title: The rich most miserable
english: Indeed experience is here so full, strong, and undeniable that it makes all other arguments needless. Appeal we therefore to fact. Are the rich and great the only happy men? And is each of them more or less happy in proportion to his measure of riches? Are they happy at all? I had nearly said they are of all men most miserable. Rich man, for once speak the truth from your heart. Speak both for yourself and for your brethren:

title: That cruel something
english: Amidst our plenty something still, to me, to you, to him is wanting. That cruel something unpossessed corrodes and leavens all the rest.

title: The night of death
english: Yes, and so it will, till your wearisome days of vanity are shut up in the night of death.

title: They cannot make you immortal
english: Surely then, to trust in riches for happiness is the greatest folly of all that are under the sun. Are you not convinced of this? Is it possible you should still expect to find happiness in money or all it can procure? What? Can silver and gold, and eating and drinking, and horses and servants, and glittering apparel, and diversions and pleasures (as they are called) make you happy? They can as soon make you immortal.

title: Trust in the living God
english: These are all dead show. Regard them not. Trust in the living God. So shall you be safe under the shadow of the Almighty. His faithfulness and truth shall be your shield and buckler (Psalm 91:4). He is a very present help in time of trouble (Psalm 46:1), such a help as can never fail. Then shall you say, if all your other friends die: The Lord lives, and blessed be my strong helper (Psalm 18:46). He shall remember you when you lie sick upon your bed. When vain is the help of man, when all the things of the earth can give no support, he will make all your bed in your sickness (Psalm 41:3). He will sweeten your pain. The consolations of God shall cause you to clap your hands in the flames. And even when this house of earth is nearly shaken down, when it is just ready to drop into the dust, he will teach you to say: O death, where is your sting? O grave, where is your victory? Thanks be to God who gives me the victory through my Lord Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 15:55-57).

title: All the springs of happiness
english: O trust in him for happiness as well as for help. All the springs of happiness are in him. Trust in him who gives us all things richly to enjoy, who of his own rich and free mercy holds them out to us, as in his own hand, that receiving them as his gift and as pledges of his love we may enjoy all that we possess (1 Timothy 6:17). It is his love that gives a relish to all we taste, puts life and sweetness into all, while every creature leads us up to the great Creator, and all earth is a scale to heaven. He transfuses the joys that are at his own right hand into all he bestows on his thankful children, who having fellowship with the Father and his Son Jesus Christ (1 John 1:3) enjoy him in all and above all.

title: A flat positive command
english: Thirdly, seek not to increase in goods. Lay not up for yourself treasures upon earth. This is a flat positive command, full as clear as you shall not commit adultery (Exodus 20:14). How then is it possible for a rich man to grow richer without denying the Lord who bought him? Yes, how can any man who has already the necessaries of life gain or aim at more and be guiltless? Lay not up, says our Lord, treasures upon earth. If in spite of this you do and will lay up money or goods which moth or rust may corrupt, or thieves break through and steal, if you will add house to house or field to field (Isaiah 5:8), why do you call yourself a Christian? You do not obey Jesus Christ. You do not design it. Why do you name yourself by his name? Why call you me Lord, Lord, says he himself, and do not the things which I say (Luke 6:46)?

title: Throw them into the sea
english: If you ask: But what must we do with our goods, seeing we have more than we have occasion to use, if we must not lay them up? Must we throw them away? I answer: If you threw them into the sea, if you were to cast them into the fire and consume them, they would be better bestowed than they are now. You cannot find so mischievous a manner of throwing them away as either the laying them up for your posterity or the laying them out upon yourselves in folly and superfluity. Of all possible methods of throwing them away, these two are the very worst, the most opposite to the gospel of Christ, and the most pernicious to your own soul.

title: Wasting a talent
english: How pernicious to your own soul the latter of these is has been excellently shown by a late writer. If we waste our money we are not only guilty of wasting a talent which God has given us, but we do ourselves this further harm: we turn this useful talent into a powerful means of corrupting ourselves, because so far as it is spent wrong, so far it is spent in the support of some wrong temper, in gratifying some vain and unreasonable desires, which as Christians we are obliged to renounce.

title: A cordial or a poison
english: As wit and fine parts cannot be only trifled away but will expose those who have them to greater follies, so money cannot be only trifled away. But if it is not used according to reason and religion, it will make people live a more silly and extravagant life than they would have done without it. If therefore you do not spend your money in doing good to others, you must spend it to the hurt of yourself. You act like one who refuses the cordial to his sick friend, which he cannot drink himself without inflaming his blood. For this is the case of superfluous money. If you give it to those who want it, it is a cordial. If you spend it upon yourself in something that you do not want, it only inflames and disorders your mind.

title: Weights upon our mind
english: In using riches where they have no real use, nor we any real want, we only use them to our great hurt, in creating unreasonable desires, in nourishing ill tempers, in indulging foolish passions, and supporting a vain turn of mind. For high eating and drinking, fine clothes and fine houses, state and equipage, gay pleasures and diversions, do all of them naturally hurt and disorder our heart. They are the food and nourishment of all the folly and weakness of our nature. They are all of them the support of something that ought not to be supported. They are contrary to that sobriety and piety of heart which relishes divine things. They are so many weights upon our mind that make us less able and less inclined to raise our thoughts and affections to things above.

title: Buying poison
english: So that money thus spent is not merely wasted or lost, but it is spent to bad purposes and miserable effects, to the corruption and disorder of our hearts, to the making us unable to follow the sublime doctrines of the gospel. It is but like keeping money from the poor to buy poison for ourselves.

title: Hoarding eyes and hands
english: Equally inexcusable are those who lay up what they do not need for any reasonable purposes. If a man had hands and eyes and feet that he could give to those who wanted them, if he should lock them up in a chest instead of giving them to his brethren who were blind and lame, should we not justly reckon him an inhuman wretch? If he should rather choose to amuse himself with hoarding them up than entitle himself to an eternal reward by giving them to those who wanted eyes and hands, might we not justly reckon him mad?

title: Locking money in chests
english: Now money has very much the nature of eyes and feet. If therefore we lock it up in chests while the poor and distressed want it for their necessary uses, we are not far from the cruelty of him who chooses rather to hoard up hands and eyes than to give them to those who want them. If we choose to lay it up rather than to entitle ourselves to an eternal reward by disposing of our money well, we are guilty of his madness who rather chooses to lock up eyes and hands than to make himself forever blessed by giving them to those who want them.

title: Robbing God and the poor
english: May not this be another reason why rich men shall so hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven? A vast majority of them are under a curse, under the peculiar curse of God, inasmuch as in the general tenor of their lives they are not only robbing God continually, embezzling and wasting their Lord's goods, and by that very means corrupting their own souls, but also robbing the poor, the hungry, the naked, wronging the widow and the fatherless, and making themselves accountable for all the want, affliction, and distress which they may but do not remove. Yes, does not the blood of all those who perish for want of what they either lay up or lay out needlessly cry against them from the earth (Genesis 4:10)? O what account will they give to him who is ready to judge both the living and the dead (1 Peter 4:5)?

title: The bank of heaven
english: The true way of employing what you do not want yourselves you may, fourthly, learn from those words of our Lord, which are the counterpart of what went before: Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust corrupts, and where thieves do not break through and steal (Matthew 6:20). Put out whatever you can spare upon better security than this world can afford. Lay up your treasures in the bank of heaven, and God shall restore them in that day. He who has pity upon the poor lends to the Lord, and what he lays out, it shall be paid him again (Proverbs 19:17). Place that, says he, to my account. However, you owe me your own self also (Philemon 1:19).

title: So much given to God
english: Give to the poor with a single eye, with an upright heart, and write: So much given to God. For inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brethren, you have done it to me (Matthew 25:40).

title: The wise steward
english: This is the part of a faithful and wise steward (Luke 12:42). Not to sell either his houses or lands or principal stock, be it more or less, unless some peculiar circumstance should require it, and not to desire or endeavor to increase it any more than to squander it away in vanity, but to employ it wholly to those wise and reasonable purposes for which his Lord has lodged it in his hands. The wise steward, after having provided his own household with what is needful for life and godliness, makes himself friends with all that remains from time to time of the mammon of unrighteousness (Luke 16:9), that when he fails they may receive him into everlasting habitations, that whenever his earthly tabernacle is dissolved, those who were before carried into Abraham's bosom, after having eaten his bread and worn the fleece of his flock and praised God for the consolation, may welcome him into paradise and into the house of God, eternal in the heavens (2 Corinthians 5:1).

title: Be rich in good works
english: We charge you therefore who are rich in this world, as having authority from our great Lord and Master, to be habitually doing good, and to live in a course of good works (1 Timothy 6:17-18). Be merciful as your Father who is in heaven is merciful (Luke 6:36), who does good and ceases not. Be merciful, how far? After your power, with all the ability which God gives (1 Peter 4:11). Make this your only measure of doing good, not any beggarly maxims or customs of the world. We charge you to be rich in good works (1 Timothy 6:18). As you have much, give plenteously. Freely you have received, freely give (Matthew 10:8), so as to lay up no treasure but in heaven. Be ready to distribute, to everyone according to his necessity (Acts 4:35). Disperse abroad, give to the poor (Psalm 112:9). Deal your bread to the hungry. Cover the naked with a garment, entertain the stranger, carry or send relief to those who are in prison. Heal the sick, not by miracle but through the blessing of God upon your seasonable support. Let the blessing of him who was ready to perish through pining want come upon you (Job 29:13). Defend the oppressed, plead the cause of the fatherless, and make the widow's heart sing for joy (Job 29:12-13).

title: Lay hold on eternal life
english: We exhort you in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ to be willing to share, to be of the same spirit (though not in the same outward state) with those believers of ancient times who remained steadfast in that blessed and holy fellowship wherein none said that anything was his own, but they had all things common (Acts 2:44-45; Acts 4:32). Be a steward, a faithful and wise steward, of God and of the poor, differing from them in these two circumstances only: that your wants are first supplied out of the portion of your Lord's goods which remains in your hands, and that you have the blessedness of giving (Acts 20:35). Thus lay up for yourselves a good foundation, not in the world which now is, but rather for the time to come, that you may lay hold on eternal life (1 Timothy 6:19). The great foundation indeed of all the blessings of God, whether temporal or eternal, is the Lord Jesus Christ, his righteousness and blood, what he has done and what he has suffered for us. And other foundation in this sense can no man lay, no not an apostle, no not an angel from heaven (Galatians 1:8). But through his merits, whatever we do in his name is a foundation for a good reward in the day when every man shall receive his own reward according to his own labor (1 Corinthians 3:8). Therefore labor, not for the food that perishes but for that which endures to everlasting life (John 6:27). Therefore whatever your hand now finds to do, do it with your might (Ecclesiastes 9:10). Therefore let

title: Snatching the golden moments
english: No fair occasion pass unheeded by. Snatching the golden moments as they fly, you by few fleeting years ensure eternity.

title: Come, you blessed
english: By patient continuance in well-doing seek for glory and honor and immortality (Romans 2:7). In a constant, zealous performance of all good works, wait for that happy hour when the King shall say: I was hungry and you gave me meat. I was thirsty and you gave me drink. I was a stranger and you took me in, naked and you clothed me. I was sick and you visited me. I was in prison and you came to me. Come, you blessed of my Father, receive the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. Matthew 25:35-36, 34.
